newsitem.title: USA: Syria's Assad may be ill - Turkish foreign minister.
newsitem.headline: Syria's Assad may be ill - Turkish foreign minister.

text.p: Turkey has received reports that Syrian President Hafez al-Assad may be very ill but has been unable to confirm them, Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller said on Thursday.
But the Cable News Network (CNN) said one of its correspondents, Rowland Evans, interviewed the 65-year-old leader in Damascus on Wednesday and that he looked in good health and spirits.

Ciller, a former Turkish prime minister, made her comment in response to a question from an Israeli reporter after she met Israel's Foreign Minister David Levy at the Turkish mission here to discuss bilateral issues and escalating violence in Israel.
The Israeli reporter asked her to comment on reports that Turkey had informed other states that Assad may be "very ill."

She responded, "Well, we have gotten some information along those lines. It is what we have heard. But we don't know if that is true or not." She declined to elaborate and quickly left the brief news conference to catch a plane to Washington.
Assad has ruled Syria since 1970 when he assumed power in a bloodless coup. He was reported to have suffered a heart attack in 1983.
In the CNN interview which will be aired on Saturday, Assad warns Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu not to stoke flames of war in the Middle East.
